Policy extract: Student Equipment Loans and Replacement (Ref: ADM/POL/14, v3.2, reviewed 02/09/2026)

14.1 Chromebook and tablet loans are made to students in Years 7–11 for home study where the Head of Year has approved the request on form ADM/F09.

14.2 Each loan is recorded in the Equipment Register (field EQ_LOAN_ID) with issue date, serial number and the signing parent or carer.

14.3 Borrowers must return the device within 5 school days of the loan end date. Devices not returned within 10 school days are reported to the Bursar as outstanding.

14.4 Where damage is reported, the Network Team inspects the device within 3 working days and grades it A (cosmetic), B (functional, repair needed) or C (write-off).

14.5 Exception: a loan may be extended beyond 10 school days without fresh approval where the student is on a Year 11 exam support plan, provided the Head of Year records the extension in the register notes field before the original end date.

14.6 Exception: grade C devices are not charged to the family where the damage is recorded as occurring on school premises.

Policy extract: BIL-P-14 Estimated Reads and Back-Billing
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Head of Billing Operations | Review due 31 March 2027

14.1 Scope
This clause applies to domestic and small business accounts where a meter reading has not been obtained within the billing period, and where a bill has been issued on an estimate.

14.2 Estimated reads
Where no actual read has been received for 90 days or more, the billing agent must raise a Read Request (RR) through the field portal before any estimated bill is reissued. The RR must state the last actual read, its date, and the Meter Serial Number (MSN) as held on the Meter Asset Register.

14.3 Back-billing limit
A supplier may not back-bill a customer for consumption older than 12 months from the date the actual read is obtained, except where clause 14.4 applies.

14.4 Exception: customer-caused access failure
Where a customer has been given at least two written access notices and the back-billed amount relates to consumption not older than 24 months, back-billing may proceed up to the 24-month limit. The agent must record the notice references (AN-number) on the account before issuing the adjusted bill.

14.5 Customer communication
Any adjusted bill above £150.00 must be preceded by a written explanation sent no less than 10 working days before the bill date. Verbal explanations do not satisfy this clause.

4. Reactive repair response
4.1 Priority 1 faults (no water, no power to a floor, lift out of service with a passenger trapped or a fire alarm fault) must be attended within 4 working hours of logging.
4.2 Priority 2 faults (single room without heating or lighting, door entry fault, toilet out of use on a floor with one other toilet) must be attended within 2 working days of logging.

4.4 Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays. Working hours are 08:00 to 17:30 Monday to Thursday and 08:00 to 16:00 Friday.
4.5 Where a job is logged after 15:00 on a working day, the clock starts at 08:00 on the next working day.

5. Closure and partial resolution
5.1 A fault is closed only when all of the following are met: (a) the defect is no longer present, (b) the reporting tenant confirms by reply to the ticket, and (c) the work order is signed off in the CAFM system.
5.2 A fault where two of the three conditions in 5.1 are met is recorded as "Partly resolved" and remains open for a further 5 working days.
5.3 A fault where only one of the three conditions in 5.1 is met is recorded as "Awaiting completion" and does not count toward response statistics.

6. Exceptions
6.1 Clause 4.3 does not apply to tenants in Suite 3 or Suite 4 during the fit-out period notified under lease schedule 2, where the repair window is extended to 15 working days.
6.2 Clause 4.5 does not apply to faults logged as Priority 1.

4.1 Where a householder application seeks retention of works already carried out, the validating officer shall record the date works were first observed by the Council, using the Enforcement Log reference where one exists.

4.2 Evidence of works completed more than four years before the application date may be accepted in lieu of a Lawful Development Certificate, provided it is corroborated by at least two independent sources (aerial imagery, dated photographs, utility connection records, or sworn statements).

4.3 Where evidence from a single source conflicts with evidence from another source, the validating officer shall give greater weight to contemporaneous records (dated imagery and utility records) over statements made after the event.

4.4 Criteria weighting: where criteria pull in different directions, the criterion relating to the safety of occupants and neighbours takes precedence over the criterion relating to the age of works. Visual amenity is weighted equally with age of works.

3. Scoring of Roof Survey Criteria

3.1 Each completed site survey is scored against four criteria: (a) roof covering condition (scale 1–5), (b) rafter/truss integrity as recorded on the structural checklist (pass / conditional / fail), (c) shading factor (percentage of annual irradiance lost, from the shading tool), and (d) customer-reported load history (free text, verified by surveyor).

3.2 Priority of criteria. Where criteria conflict, structural integrity (3.1(b)) takes precedence over all other criteria. A "fail" result cannot be overridden by any other criterion except as set out in clause 5.3. Shading and roof covering condition are weighted equally with each other and are secondary to structural integrity.

3.3 Survey observations recorded by the surveyor on the handheld device take precedence over third-party reports supplied by the customer, unless the third-party report is an engineer's certificate issued within the preceding 24 months.

4. Installation Eligibility

4.1 A roof is eligible for standard installation where the structural checklist reads "pass" and roof covering condition is 3 or above.

4.2 A roof reading "conditional" under 3.1(b) requires a structural addendum (form SC-F7) signed by a Chartered Engineer before scheduling.

4.3 Roofs with shading factor above 22% are referred to the Design desk for string layout review before quotation. Referral does not by itself make a roof ineligible.

5. Exceptions and Reinstatement

5.1 Installations previously declined under 4.1 may be re-surveyed once the recorded defect has been remedied and evidenced.

5.2 Re-surveys must be carried out by a surveyor other than the original.

5.3 Where an engineer's certificate under 3.3 confirms that a rafter defect recorded as "fail" has been fully remediated, the Head of Surveys may approve installation provided that: (i) the certificate post-dates the original survey by at least 60 days; (ii) the rafter area concerned has had no further reported incident; and (iii) the roof covering scores 4 or above. Approval must be recorded on form SC-F9 with the reference of the certificate.

6. Records

6.1 All survey outcomes are held on the job record in the CRM under the field names listed in Annex B.

CASE NOTE — Job ref SC/2026/08817
Site: 14 Larkhill Close, Wexcombe Green. Customer: M. Dhillon.
Original survey: 17/07/2026, surveyor J. Pemberton (handheld). Checklist: rafter integrity FAIL, rear north-west slope, joist 9 and 10 noted soft at eaves. Roof covering 4. Shading factor 19%. Customer load history: "re-roofed and re-timbered 2019" (not verified).

The letter does not state the certificate was issued by a Chartered Engineer. 4. Demurrage: chargeable period and liability

4.1 Demurrage is chargeable by the carrier for each full or part day a laden or empty container remains in the terminal beyond the free time stated on the carrier's booking confirmation. Free time begins at 00:00 on the day after discharge is recorded at the terminal gate-out system.

4.2 The company is liable for demurrage only where the delay is attributable to the consignee, the customs broker or the company's own booking actions, as recorded under clause 4.4.

4.3 Where a carrier invoice is received, the Booking Desk shall match it against the gate-in and gate-out timestamps from the terminal portal and record the match result in field DEM-MATCH on the shipment file within two working days of receipt.

4.4 Each delay shall be assigned one cause code from the following list: CONS (consignee not ready), CUST (customs hold or inspection), BOOK (booking error or late instruction), CARR (carrier or terminal fault), WTHR (weather or port closure). Cause codes must be supported by at least one dated observation on the shipment file.

4.5 EXCEPTION: Where a carrier or terminal fault (CARR) is confirmed in writing by the terminal operator, the company is not liable for the resulting demurrage and the charge shall be referred to the carrier for credit. Written confirmation must be attached to the shipment file before the cause code is set.

4.6 EXCEPTION: For WTHR delays, liability is shared equally between the company and the consignee, unless the consignee has been notified of the closure in writing within 24 hours, in which case the consignee bears the full charge.

4.7 Verbal confirmation from terminal staff is not sufficient evidence for clause 4.5 and must be recorded only as a provisional note pending written confirmation.

---

Prepared by: R. Okonkwo, Booking Desk | Date: 27 October 2026

Container MSKU-4471926 discharged on 9 October 2026. Terminal gate-out system shows gate-out on 19 October at 14:52. Free time per carrier confirmation was 4 days from the day after discharge. Carrier invoice INV-88213 claims 6 days demurrage at £95 per day, total £570.

Brennan, 15 October, says the fault was "probably" the terminal's and that a written statement would follow. No written statement is on file as at today.

Consignee (Ashcroft Tools Ltd) emailed on 13 October stating their warehouse was not ready to receive until the 18th. This email is on file. No written WTHR notice was sent by the company to the consignee.

Cause codes not yet set. Accounts Payable has asked whether the £570 can be held pending the outcome. The carrier's invoice was received 21 October, so the two-working-day matching window under clause 4.3 closes on 23 October.

7.1 Scope
This section applies to all reactive requests logged through the helpdesk portal (ticket prefix HHF-) or the 24-hour line that relate to water ingress, plant alarms, lift faults or security door failures in Blocks A, B and C.

7.2 Response times
7.2.1 Priority 1 (risk to life, active leak into electrical distribution, lift entrapment): attend on site within 60 minutes of logging.
7.2.2 Priority 2 (active leak without electrical risk, boiler lockout, heating failure in occupied areas): attend within 4 working hours.
7.2.3 Priority 3 (all other reactive faults): attend within 2 working days.
7.2.4 Response time runs from the time logged on the portal or the time the 24-hour line call is answered, whichever is earlier. Time is recorded in local time (Europe/London) and is not converted to UTC.

7.3 Out-of-hours
7.3.1 Working hours are 07:30 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays.
7.3.2 Priority 1 calls received outside working hours are dispatched to the on-call contractor (Castellan Mechanical Services) without further approval.
7.3.3 Priority 2 calls received after 18:00 on a Friday, or at any time on a weekend or bank holiday, are held until 07:30 on the next working day unless the Duty Officer approves earlier dispatch.

7.4 Plant alarm thresholds
7.4.1 Sump pump high-level alarm: trigger at 350 mm. Pump run-time above 40 minutes in any 60-minute period is logged as a Priority 2 fault.
7.4.2 Chilled water return temperature: alarm above 14.0 °C. Readings are logged in °C on the BMS; contractor reports may quote °F.
7.4.3 Lift car door dwell: any door held open beyond 45 seconds in service is logged as Priority 3 unless it recurs three times in a rolling 24-hour period, in which case it is re-coded Priority 2.

7.5 Exceptions
7.5.1 Clauses 7.2.2 and 7.3.3 do not apply where water is entering a plant room housing the main switchboard. Such calls are Priority 1 regardless of time or day.
7.5.2 Where the on-call contractor attends and records that the fault is caused by a tenant fit-out works item, the response category is held at the original priority for reporting purposes only.

7.6 Records
7.6.1 Each call-out record must show: ticket reference, time logged, time attended, priority, attending engineer, and any BMS reading relied upon.
7.6.2 Monthly totals of call-outs by block are reported to the Facilities Manager by the fifth working day of the following month.

Extract (version 3, adopted 14 May 2024; review due May 2027)

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to any temporary use of land within the parish for markets, fairs, funfairs, or outdoor events where attendance is expected to exceed 150 persons at any one time.

2. Application requirements
2.1 Applicants must submit form TU2 no less than 42 calendar days before the first day of the proposed use.
2.2 Each application must state the expected peak attendance, the number of days in the proposed period, and the proposed hours of operation.
2.3 Where a previous temporary use on the same site has been permitted in the preceding 24 months, the applicant must provide the attendance figures recorded for that use.

3. Assessment criteria
3.1 Peak attendance shall be measured against the site capacity stated in the Site Register, expressed as persons per 100 square metres of usable ground.
3.2 Where recorded attendance at a previous use exceeded the stated peak attendance by more than 15%, the application shall be referred to committee regardless of value under clause 4.1.
3.3 Noise assessments shall be provided in dB(A) Leq over a 1-hour period, and in dB(A) LAeq,T over the full event period where the event runs beyond 22:00.

4. Determination
4.1 Applications for events of up to 3 days, with peak attendance below 500, may be determined under delegated authority by the Clerk.
4.2 All other applications shall be determined by the Planning & Licensing Committee.

5. Exceptions
5.1 Clause 4.1 does not apply where the site lies within 200 metres of a residential boundary.
5.2 Notwithstanding clause 2.1, the Clerk may accept an application submitted less than 42 days before the proposed use where the event is a registered charity fundraiser and the Clerk is satisfied that the delay was not caused by the applicant.

7. Proration basis
7.1 Proration is calculated on a per-day basis using the number of days in the billing period in which the change takes effect. Days are counted from the effective timestamp (UTC) to the end of the billing period, inclusive of the day of change.
7.2 Where a billing period spans a calendar month end, the period length used is the actual number of days in that billing period, not the calendar month.
7.3 Amounts are rounded to two decimal places at line level. Rounding differences are not carried forward.

8. Upgrades
8.1 An upgrade takes effect immediately. The charge is the prorated difference between the old and new monthly list price for the unused portion of the period.
8.2 Where the account is on an annual plan, the proration basis is 365 days and the prorated amount is expressed in monthly-equivalent terms before tax.

9. Downgrades and seat reductions
9.1 A downgrade takes effect at the next renewal date. No credit is issued for the unused portion of the current period.
9.2 Exception (9.2a): where a downgrade is requested within 48 hours of an upgrade on the same account, the downgrade is treated as effective from the upgrade timestamp and the unused portion is credited at the upgraded rate.
9.3 Exception (9.3b): seat reductions on enterprise accounts with more than 50 seats are processed on the 1st of the following month, regardless of request date.

10. Service credits
10.1 Service credits are calculated as a percentage of the monthly fee for the affected service. Credit percentage is set by Table 10.1 using the measured uptime ratio (uptime minutes over scheduled minutes in the month).
10.2 Credits are capped at 25% of the monthly fee per affected service.

Extract: Sections 4 to 6

4. Triggers for review

4.1 A member account is referred to the Fraud Prevention queue where any one of the following applies within a rolling 30-day window:
(a) more than 3 reward redemptions, each exceeding 1,500 points;
(b) points credited from store transactions where the till receipt has been voided or reissued more than twice;
(c) a change of registered mobile number followed by a redemption within 72 hours.

4.2 Account-level scores are taken from the nightly scoring job (job ref NS-LP-0212). A score is the mean of the three most recent daily risk readings for the account. Readings below 40 are not used in the mean because they are recorded only as provisional.

5. Reversal of rewards

5.1 Where a referral under 4.1 is substantiated, the Loyalty Team may reverse any reward issued in the 90 days preceding the referral date, up to a maximum of 4,800 points per account per calendar month.

5.2 Points are reversed at the redemption value in force on the date of issue, not the date of reversal. Reversals are posted to the member ledger as type RVS with a reference beginning HHG-RV.

5.3 Points-to-currency conversion for any reversal quoted to a member is 100 points = £1.25.

6. Exceptions

6.1 Clause 5.1 does not apply where the member is aged 70 or over, or where the member holds a Harvest Gold tier status for 24 consecutive months or more.

6.2 Where a 6.1 exception applies, the referral is closed with reason code EX-6 and the case is returned to the store operations team for goodwill review under policy HHG-OPS/POL/0031.

6.3 Exceptions must be approved by a Fraud Prevention Lead before the case is closed. Approval references take the form FPL-YYYY-NNNN.
